mainTopic: The holy מנה, רבי חנינא's questions to רבי אליעזר, and the rule that a בכור must be the same species as its mother (פטר חמור and kosher animals)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a math puzzle about יחזקאל's 'holy מנה.' The גמרא concludes that the holy מנה was double, and that measures may be enlarged by up to a sixth counted from the outside. רבי חנינא then reports several questions he asked רבי אליעזר. He asked why only donkeys have the בכור law: it is a גזירת הכתוב, and donkeys also carried Israel's wealth out of מצרים. He also asked what the names רפידים and שטים mean. Each time רבי אליעזר says 'it is just its name,' while רבי יהושע reads each name as a hint about the people's sin. A new משנה then teaches that פטר חמור applies only when both mother and baby are donkeys. It adds that an animal's kashrus follows its mother. The גמרא shows that our תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי learn the 'same kind' rule from different verses, and it works through a long צריכא about why ox, lamb and goat are all mentioned. The amud ends with a ברייתא suggesting that horses and camels might still be redeemed with any item, and the reply comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse's total is far too big for a מנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the 60 shekels in יחזקאל's verse equal 240 dinars, much more than a normal מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that comes out to two hundred and forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the verse in יחזקאל that was just quoted. Its numbers (20 + 25 + 15 shekels = 60 shekels) add up to 240 dinars, which does not fit a 'מנה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each shekel (סלע) is worth 4 dinars, so 60 shekels equal 240 dinars. A normal מנה is only 100 dinars, which is 25 shekels. The verse calls 60 shekels a 'מנה,' and that seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of money or weight, normally worth 100 dinars (25 shekels)
Two hundred and forty
'But look!', which opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The number 240 is in dinars, not shekels. The verse itself speaks of shekels (60 of them). Keep the two units apart: 1 shekel = 4 dinars.

phrases.english: But that comes to two hundred and forty [dinars]!
phrases.notes: 60 shekels × 4 dinars = 240 dinars, while a normal מנה is 100 dinars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the verse in יחזקאל quoted on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse's sum (60 shekels = 240 dinars) does not match the standard value of a מנה (100 dinars).

steps.title: The holy מנה was a double מנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the problem: the מנה of the Sanctuary was twice the size of a regular מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the מנה of the Sanctuary was a double מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the math problem. It concludes that the 'holy מנה' was double the normal size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A double מנה is 200 dinars, which is 50 shekels. That brings us much closer to the verse's 60 shekels. The remaining 10 shekels still need an explanation, and the next step supplies it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it must be that
Learn from it; we can conclude
The holy מנה, the one used for Sanctuary matters
Doubled

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ מָנֶה כָּפוּל הָיָה.
phrases.english: the מנה of the Sanctuary was a doubled מנה.
phrases.notes: Double means 200 dinars, which is 50 shekels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the unit: the holy מנה has a different value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A 'מנה' in the verse means a standard 100-dinar מנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Sanctuary מנה was double, 200 dinars (50 shekels).

steps.title: Measures may be enlarged, but only by one-sixth counted from the outside
steps.stepSummary: From the extra 10 shekels, the גמרא learns that measures may be increased by up to a sixth, and that the sixth is measured from the final total.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it that we may add to measures, but we may not add more than a sixth. And learn from it that the sixth is counted from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the leftover 10 shekels, the gap between 50 and 60. From this gap it draws two more rules about enlarging official measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse made the מנה 60 instead of 50, which shows that a community may enlarge its measures. Since the increase was only 10 out of 60, the limit is one-sixth. Ten is a sixth of the new total (60) but a fifth of the original (50), so the sixth is counted 'from the outside,' meaning from the final total.

keyTerms.meaning: We may increase the measures
One-sixth
More than; beyond
From the outside, meaning counted from the final total

steps.whatToRemember: The holy מנה was double: 50 shekels. יחזקאל's 60 teaches that measures may be enlarged by up to a sixth, where the sixth is a sixth of the new total (מלבר).
steps.confusionAlert: 'A sixth from the outside' does NOT mean adding a sixth of the original amount. It means the added part is a sixth of the final sum. That works out to adding a fifth of the original (10 added to 50 gives 60).
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of a 'sixth from the outside' (שתותא מלבר) comes up elsewhere in הלכה, for example in measuring adjustments. Here it is derived from a verse.

phrases.english: And learn from it: we may add to measures,
phrases.notes: The מנה grew from 50 to 60.

phrases.english: but we may not add more than a sixth,
and learn from it that the sixth is from the outside.
phrases.notes: 10 is a sixth of 60 (the final total), and a fifth of 50 (the original).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the resolution by accounting for the remaining 10 shekels and drawing halachic lessons.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Holy מנה = 50 shekels. Communities may enlarge measures by up to one-sixth of the new total.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks why only donkeys have firstborn rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports asking רבי אליעזר why firstborn donkeys differ from firstborn horses and camels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: I asked רבי אליעזר in the great study hall: What makes firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the math discussion and goes back to the law of פטר חמור. It sets up a question that רבי חנינא put to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horses and camels are non-kosher animals, just like donkeys. Yet only the firstborn donkey must be redeemed. The question asks for the reason behind this one exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn donkeys
How are they different?
The great study hall (literally, the great house of sitting)
Horses and camels

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּבֵית מוֹתְבָא רַבָּא,
phrases.english: I asked Rabbi Eliezer in the great study hall:
what makes firstborn donkeys different
from firstborn horses and camels?
phrases.notes: These are other non-kosher animals, which have no redemption law.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּבֵית מוֹתְבָא רַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the money calculation back to the main subject of פטר חמור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason donkeys alone, among non-kosher animals, have firstborn sanctity.

steps.title: A Torah decree, and the donkeys helped at the Exodus
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that it is a גזירת הכתוב, and adds that donkeys carried the wealth of מצרים for the Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: It is a decree of the Torah. And also, the donkeys helped the Jews when they left מצרים, because every single Jew had ninety Nubian donkeys loaded with the silver and gold of מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a two-part answer to רבי חנינא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His main answer is that the Torah simply decreed it, so no reason is required. He then adds a supporting idea: donkeys earned this honor because they carried the riches of מצרים for every Jew at יציאת מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree of the verse; a Torah rule given without a stated reason
And furthermore
They helped
Nubian (Libyan) donkeys, considered high-quality

phrases.english: He said to me: It is a Torah decree,
and furthermore, they [the donkeys] helped Israel
at the time of their going out from Egypt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָךְ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: for there was not a single one of Israel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עִמּוֹ תִּשְׁעִים חֲמוֹרִים לוּבִים
phrases.english: who did not have with him ninety Nubian donkeys
loaded with the silver and gold of Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a גזירת הכתוב. In addition, donkeys earned it by carrying the wealth of מצרים at יציאת מצרים.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks what רפידים means
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports a second question he asked רבי אליעזר: the meaning of the name רפידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also asked him: What is the meaning of the word 'רפידים'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא sets up a second, unrelated question he put to רבי אליעזר. It asks about the place-name רפידים, where עמלק attacked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether 'רפידים' carries a hidden meaning or is just a name. It is included here because it was part of the same conversation.

keyTerms.meaning: I asked him
What is the meaning of the term?
רפידים, the place where עמלק fought Israel (שמות יז:ח)

phrases.english: And I further asked him:
What is the meaning of the term 'Rephidim'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question from the same conversation between רבי חנינא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the name רפידים has an interpretive meaning.

steps.title: רפידים is simply the place's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that רפידים is just the name of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: רפידים is its name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers plainly that 'רפידים' is the actual name of the location and carries no hidden message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He rejects reading a hint into the name. This plain reading sets up the next step, where the גמרא shows that other תנאים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Its name

phrases.english: And he said to me: Rephidim is its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רפידים is the place's literal name.

steps.title: This is a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the meaning of רפידים is disputed by תנאים. רבי יהושע reads it as a hint that the Jews became lax in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: רפידים is its name. רבי יהושע says: it hints that they loosened their hold on the words of the Torah, as it says: 'The fathers did not turn back to their children because of weakness of hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comments that רבי אליעזר's answer is one side of a known dispute between תנאים. It then presents the other side, from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר takes the name literally. רבי יהושע connects 'רפידים' to the root רפה (weak or loose): at רפידים the Jews grew slack in Torah (the place where עמלק attacked). He supports the wordplay with the word 'רפיון' in a verse from ירמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים
That they loosened (weakened) themselves
And so it says, introducing a supporting verse
Weakness (slackness) of hands

steps.whatToRemember: רפידים: according to רבי אליעזר it is just a name. According to רבי יהושע it hints at רפיון, slackness in Torah, using the word רפיון from ירמיה.

phrases.english: This is like [a dispute of] tannaim:
Rabbi Eliezer says: Rephidim is its name;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁרִיפּוּ עַצְמָן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: [it is called so] because they slackened themselves from the words of Torah,
phrases.notes: Wordplay: רפידים and רִפּוּ (slackened).

phrases.english: and so it says:
'The fathers did not turn back to the children
because of weakness of hands.'
phrases.notes: ירמיה מז:ג. It shows the root רפה meaning slackness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places רבי אליעזר's answer within a broader dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר holds that רפידים is a literal name. רבי יהושע reads it as a hint at slackness in Torah.

steps.title: Third question: what does the name שטים mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports another question he asked רבי אליעזר: what is the meaning of the name שטים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also asked him: What is the meaning of the word 'שטים'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא is still listing his questions to רבי אליעזר. Now he asks about the place name שטים, where the Jews sinned with the daughters of מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question follows the same pattern as the רפידים question. He is asking whether the name is only a label or whether it hints at something that happened there.

keyTerms.meaning: And I also asked him
The meaning of a word or term
Shittim, the place where the Jews camped and sinned (במדבר כה)

phrases.english: And furthermore I asked him:
What is the meaning of the term 'Shittim'?
phrases.notes: From the verse 'וישב ישראל בשטים' (במדבר כה:א).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of questions רבי חנינא asked, right after the רפידים question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the name שטים meaningful, or is it only the name of the place?

steps.title: Answer: שטים is just its name
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that שטים is simply the name of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: שטים is its name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the same kind of answer he gave for רפידים. It is just a place name, with no hidden message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר stays consistent. He does not read hints into place names. This sets up the גמרא's next move, which shows that other תנאים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Its name (that is all it is)

phrases.english: And he said to me: Shittim is its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שטים is just the place's name and carries no hidden meaning.

steps.title: A dispute: plain name or a hint of foolishness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the meaning of שטים is a תנאים dispute. רבי אליעזר says it is just the name. רבי יהושע says it hints that they busied themselves with שטות (nonsense).
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: שטים is its name. רבי יהושע says: It is called that because they busied themselves with matters of nonsense.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did with רפידים, the גמרא points out that this answer matches one side of an older argument. רבי יהושע reads the name as a hint about the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע connects שטים with the word שטות, meaning foolishness. This refers to the immorality and idol worship at that place. So the name describes what the people did there.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים
They busied themselves with
Nonsense or foolishness (here: immorality and idol worship)

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between tanna'im:
Rabbi Eliezer says: Shittim is its name,
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
That they were engaged in matters of nonsense.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: שטים sounds like שטות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places רבי אליעזר's answer inside a תנאים dispute, the same pattern as step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: שטים is just a name. רבי יהושע: it hints that they were busy with שטות.

steps.title: Another dispute about the same sin: what 'they called' means
steps.stepSummary: The same תנאים argue about the verse 'וַתִּקְרֶאןָ לָעָם לְזִבְחֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶן'. רבי אליעזר says naked women met them. רבי יהושע says they all became בעלי קריין.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the verse 'And they called the people to the offerings of their gods': רבי אליעזר says naked women met them. רבי יהושע says they all became people who had a seminal emission.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying with the story of שטים, the גמרא brings another argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. This one is about the next verse, which describes how the women drew the Jews in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions read the word וַתִּקְרֶאןָ as a hint. רבי אליעזר links it to קרה, meaning 'happened upon': the women met them unclothed. רבי יהושע links it to קרי: the people all became impure through lust.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they called' (read here as a hint)
Naked women
They met or encountered
People who had a seminal emission

phrases.english: 'And they called the people to the offerings of their gods' (Numbers 25:2) —
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Naked women encountered them,
phrases.notes: Reading the word like קרה, to happen upon.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
That they all became those who experienced seminal emissions.
phrases.notes: Reading the word like קרי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second dispute between the same תנאים about the same episode at שטים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: naked women met them. רבי יהושע: they all became בעלי קריין.
steps.whatToRemember: The questions רבי חנינא asked רבי אליעזר (donkeys, רפידים, שטים) end here. In each name case, רבי אליעזר says 'it is just the name', and רבי יהושע reads a hint about the people's sin.

steps.title: New משנה: a firstborn donkey requires both mother and baby to be donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a cow that gives birth to something like a donkey, or a donkey that gives birth to something like a horse, is פטור from בכורה. The Torah says 'פטר חמור' twice, which teaches that both the mother and the baby must be donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A cow that gave birth to a kind of donkey, and a donkey that gave birth to a kind of horse, are exempt from the firstborn law. This is because the Torah says 'firstborn of a donkey' two times. It does not apply until the mother is a donkey and the baby is a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It asks what happens when an animal gives birth to a baby that looks like a different species. It rules that the law of פטר חמור applies only when both mother and baby are donkeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases. In the first, the mother is not a donkey (a cow). In the second, the baby is not a donkey (it looks like a horse). Since the Torah repeats 'פטר חמור' twice, the משנה reads it as two requirements: the one giving birth must be a donkey, and the one born must be a donkey. If either is missing, there is no obligation of פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (a new משנה begins here)
Exempt from the firstborn law
A firstborn donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
The one giving birth (the mother)
The one born (the baby)

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases are exempt, but for different reasons. With the cow, the mother is not a donkey. With the donkey, the baby is not a donkey. Each case breaks a different one of the two requirements.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for פטר חמור: you need a donkey born from a donkey. This connects to the earlier question of why only donkeys, and not horses or camels, have this law.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts,
and a donkey that gave birth to a horse of sorts —
are exempt from the firstborn obligation,
as it is stated: 'firstborn of a donkey', 'firstborn of a donkey'
phrases.notes: שמות יג:יג and שמות לד:כ.

phrases.english: two times,
teaching that it does not apply unless the one giving birth is a donkey
and the one born is a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves from the אגדה back to the laws of בכורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פטר חמור applies only when both the mother and the newborn are donkeys, learned from the double mention of 'פטר חמור'.

steps.title: The משנה asks: what about eating such animals?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what the kashrus status is of a baby that looks like a different kind of animal than its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is their status regarding eating?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה turns from the firstborn law to a related question: may such an animal be eaten? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having ruled that species matters for בכורה, the משנה now asks whether looks or mother decides kashrus. This is not a challenge. It simply opens the next rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding eating

phrases.english: And what is their status with regard to eating?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the cases of step 13 (a baby unlike its mother) to the question of kashrus.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is an animal born looking like another species kosher or not?

steps.title: Kashrus follows the mother
steps.stepSummary: A kosher animal that gives birth to something that looks non-kosher: the baby may be eaten. A non-kosher animal that gives birth to something that looks kosher: the baby may not be eaten. What comes from the טמא is טמא, and what comes from the טהור is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kosher animal that gave birth to something like a non-kosher animal: it is permitted to eat. A non-kosher animal that gave birth to something like a kosher animal: it is forbidden to eat. This is because what comes out of the non-kosher is non-kosher, and what comes out of the kosher is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. Whether an animal is kosher depends on its mother, not on what it looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby's appearance does not decide anything. The rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' means a baby takes the status of the animal it came from. Notice the contrast: for בכורה, the baby's species matters too. For kashrus, only the mother counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher animal
A non-kosher animal
Like a kind of (looks like)
What comes from the non-kosher is non-kosher

steps.confusionAlert: Don't judge by looks. A baby that looks like a camel but was born to a kosher cow is kosher. A baby that looks like a cow but was born to a camel is not kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: For בכורה of a donkey, both mother and baby must be donkeys. For kashrus, the status follows the mother: היוצא מן הטמא טמא, והיוצא מן הטהור טהור.

phrases.english: A kosher animal that gave birth
to a non-kosher animal of sorts —
it is permitted to eat,
and a non-kosher animal that gave birth to a kosher animal of sorts —
it is forbidden to eat,
because that which emerges from the non-kosher is non-kosher,
and that which emerges from the kosher is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kashrus follows the mother: the offspring of a kosher animal is kosher, and the offspring of a non-kosher animal is not kosher, whatever it looks like.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' is a basic rule of kashrus. The גמרא will soon look for its source and its limits.

steps.title: Quoting a משנה about a ewe that births a goat-like lamb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה from elsewhere: a ewe that births a goat-like animal, or a goat that births a ewe-like animal, is exempt from בכורה. If the baby has some of its mother's signs, it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: a ewe that gave birth to a goat-type animal, or a goat that gave birth to a ewe-type animal, is exempt from בכורה. But if the baby has some of the mother's features, it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה from later in the מסכתא so it can look for its source. This sets up the next question, 'where do we learn this from?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ewes and goats are both kosher animals that are normally subject to בכורה. Even so, the baby is exempt when it does not look like its mother's species. The exemption disappears once the baby has even some of the mother's signs.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere (in another place)
A ewe (female sheep)
A goat of sorts, an animal that looks like a goat
Exempt from the laws of a firstborn animal
Some of the identifying features (here, features of the mother)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the previous kashrus משנה (Step 15). This case is about בכורה, not about whether the baby may be eaten. Both animals here are kosher anyway.

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there (in a mishna):
A ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts,
phrases.notes: The baby looks like a goat, not like its mother.

phrases.english: and a goat that gave birth to a ewe of sorts
is exempt from the firstborn obligation,
and if it has some of the signs (of its mother)
it is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel משנה about mismatched species and בכורה. It connects to Step 13's case of a cow that birthed a donkey-like animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A kosher animal's baby that looks like a different species is exempt from בכורה. If it has some of its mother's signs, it is obligated.

steps.title: Asking for the source of this rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the משנה's rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things need a source. First, why a ewe-goat mismatch exempts the baby. Second, why some signs of the mother bring the obligation back.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for exempting a species-mismatched baby from בכורה.

steps.title: רב יהודה learns it from 'firstborn of an ox, lamb, goat'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings the verse 'אך בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז'. Each phrase teaches that the mother and the baby must be the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The verse says, 'But the firstborn of an ox.' This means the mother must be an ox and its firstborn an ox. 'The firstborn of a lamb' means the mother must be a lamb and its firstborn a lamb. 'The firstborn of a goat' means the mother must be a goat and its firstborn a goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question with a verse. Each animal named in the verse must give birth to its own kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בכור' together with each species name is read as a requirement that both mother and baby be that species. So a ewe that births a goat-like baby fails 'בכור כשב'. It also fails 'בכור עז', because the mother is not a goat.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
The firstborn of an ox (cattle)
A lamb / sheep
And its firstborn

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: As the verse states:
"But the firstborn of an ox"
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:יז

phrases.english: that it should be an ox and its firstborn an ox;
"the firstborn of a lamb"
that it should be a lamb and its firstborn a lamb;
"the firstborn of a goat"
that it should be a goat and its firstborn a goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנא הני מילי question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'אך בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז' requires that mother and baby be the same species.

steps.title: The word 'But' makes an exception for partial signs
steps.stepSummary: One might think a baby with only some of the mother's signs is also exempt. The word 'אך' teaches a distinction: such a baby is a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the baby is exempt even if it has some of the mother's signs. Therefore the verse says 'But' (אך), which makes a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The derivation continues and explains the second half of the משנה. A baby with some of the mother's features is still obligated as a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading only 'בכור שור' etc., we might demand a full match and exempt any baby that is not a perfect copy of its mother. The word 'אך' limits that exemption. Partial resemblance is enough to keep the baby inside the category of בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a possible but wrong assumption)
Therefore the verse says (to teach otherwise)
But / only, a limiting word in the verse
It made a distinction

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules from one verse: (1) mother and baby must be the same species for בכורה ('בכור שור/כשב/עז'); (2) if the baby has some of the mother's signs, it still counts ('אך' חילק).

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין?
phrases.english: One might think: even if it has some of the signs (it is exempt)?
The verse states: "But" — it made a distinction.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's derivation by sourcing the משנה's 'מקצת סימנין — חייב' clause.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אך' makes a distinction, so a baby with some of the mother's signs is obligated in בכורה.

steps.title: Challenge: our משנה used 'פטר פטר' for this rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה: the תנא of our משנה learned the cow-and-donkey case from the double 'פטר'. Why does רב יהודה need a different verse?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא (of our משנה) cites 'פטר' 'פטר' for the case of a cow (that gave birth to a donkey-like animal)! So why use a different verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty against רב יהודה's source. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13 our משנה learned from the double 'פטר חמור' that both mother and baby must be donkeys. That is the same idea of a species match, and it was applied to a cow that birthed a donkey-like animal. If the double 'פטר' already teaches this, why does רב יהודה need 'בכור שור/כשב/עז'?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that… (introduces a challenge)
The one that opens the womb, i.e., firstborn (from 'פטר חמור')
He cites it / takes it (as the source)
A cow

phrases.english: But doesn't the tanna (cite) "firstborn," "firstborn"
phrases.notes: The double 'פטר חמור' from שמות, used in our משנה (Step 13).

phrases.english: with regard to a cow!
phrases.notes: The case of a cow that gave birth to a donkey-like animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא פֶּטֶר פֶּטֶר קָנָסֵיב לַהּ לְפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's choice of source by pointing to the source our משנה used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's derivation from 'אך בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה already uses the double 'פטר' to teach that mother and baby must match, and applies it to a cow. So רב יהודה's separate verse seems unnecessary, or it conflicts with the תנא's source.

steps.title: רב יהודה is following רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה's reading of the verse is not his own invention. It comes from a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי, which reads each phrase as requiring the mother and baby to be the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said it according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, as a ברייתא teaches. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: 'But the firstborn of an ox' means it must be an ox and its firstborn an ox. 'The firstborn of a sheep' means it must be a sheep and its firstborn a sheep. 'Or the firstborn of a goat' means it must be a goat and its firstborn a goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20. רב יהודה uses a different verse because he holds like a different תנא, רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was: our משנה learns the rule from the double 'פטר', so why does רב יהודה need 'אך בכור שור'? The answer is that two תנאים learned the same rule from two different verses. רב יהודה is simply quoting the source of רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (early sage) whose ברייתא is quoted here
As a ברייתא teaches (a teaching of the תנאים that is outside the משנה)
And its firstborn (the baby)
Unless it is / only when it is

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב יהודה is arguing with the משנה on his own. An אמורא like רב יהודה is simply taking the side of an existing תנא.

phrases.english: He (רב יהודה) says it according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: The answer to the challenge

phrases.english: as a ברייתא teaches:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"But the firstborn of an ox" —

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר,
phrases.english: not unless the mother is an ox and its firstborn is an ox,
"the firstborn of a sheep" —

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא כֶּשֶׂב וּבְכוֹרוֹ כֶּשֶׂב,
phrases.english: not unless the mother is a sheep and its firstborn is a sheep,
"or the firstborn of a goat" —

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא עֵז וּבְכוֹרוֹ עֵז.
phrases.english: not unless the mother is a goat and its firstborn is a goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement follows a different תנא who uses a different verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה invented a second source when the משנה already had one
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה is following רבי יוסי הגלילי, who learns the rule from 'אך בכור שור'

steps.title: The ברייתא also teaches the 'some signs' exception from אך
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One might think a baby with only some of its mother's signs is also exempt. The word 'אך' limits the rule, so such a baby is a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the rule applies even if the baby has some of the mother's signs. That is why the verse says 'אך': it makes a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי. It shows that the second half of רב יהודה's teaching (step 19) also comes from this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אך' is a limiting word. Here it cuts back the 'same kind' rule. The baby does not need to match its mother completely. Having some of the mother's signs is enough to make it a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Some of the identifying signs (of the mother)
Therefore the verse says
It made a distinction (it limited the rule)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין?
phrases.english: Might one think that even if it has some of the mother's signs, it is exempt?
The verse says: "But" (אך) — it makes a distinction.
phrases.notes: So a baby with some of the mother's signs is a בכור

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completing the attribution: the full teaching of רב יהודה appears in the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parts of רב יהודה's teaching come from רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: What is the disagreement between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what our תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי actually disagree about, since they agree on the rule but use different verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It asks what deeper idea makes the two תנאים choose different verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that a baby that does not look like its mother is not a בכור. The only difference is which verse is the main source. The גמרא wants to know the reason behind that choice.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the attribution in step 21 by asking for the root of the disagreement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason the two תנאים derive the same law from different verses

steps.title: Our תנא: the Torah wrote it about the donkey
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה's תנא holds that the Torah stated the rule about the firstborn donkey, which has קדושת דמים. The same rule then applies to kosher animals, which have קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of our משנה holds: the Torah revealed the rule regarding value-sanctity (the donkey), and the same is true for body-sanctity (kosher animals).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains our תנא's view. The Torah wrote the 'same kind' rule about the donkey (the double 'פטר'), and our תנא extends it to kosher animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn donkey has קדושת דמים, because only its value is holy and it is redeemed with a lamb. A kosher firstborn has קדושת הגוף, because the animal itself is holy and goes on the מזבח. For our תנא, the Torah's main statement is about the donkey, and kosher animals are learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of our משנה
The Torah (lit. 'the Merciful One') revealed
Holiness of value only (like the firstborn donkey, which is redeemed)
Holiness of the body itself (like a kosher firstborn, which is offered)
And the same law applies

steps.confusionAlert: Remember which is which. The donkey (פטר חמור) has קדושת דמים. The kosher ox, sheep, or goat has קדושת הגוף.

phrases.english: The tanna of our mishna holds:
The Torah revealed the rule regarding value-sanctity (the donkey),
and the same applies to body-sanctity (kosher animals).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First half of the answer to step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our תנא sees the donkey verse as the main source and extends it to kosher animals

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the Torah wrote it about kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that the Torah stated the rule about kosher animals, which have קדושת הגוף. The donkey, which has קדושת דמים, is learned from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: the Torah revealed the rule regarding body-sanctity (kosher animals), and the same is true for value-sanctity (the donkey). He learns value-sanctity from body-sanctity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer with the opposite view. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'אך בכור שור' as the main source and extends it to the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a mirror image of our תנא's view. Both agree the rule covers both kinds of בכור. They disagree only about which case the Torah wrote directly and which is learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he learns / derives

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a baby that does not look like its mother is not a בכור, unless it has some of the mother's signs. Our תנא learns it from the donkey (קדושת דמים, the double 'פטר'). רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from the kosher animals (קדושת הגוף, 'אך בכור שור'). רב יהודה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רב יהודה needed a separate verse. The challenge in step 20 is fully answered: two verses reflect two views about which kind of holiness is the main case.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
The Torah revealed the rule regarding body-sanctity (kosher animals),
and the same applies to value-sanctity (the donkey),
and he learns value-sanctity from body-sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the answer to step 23, the mirror image of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי sees the kosher-animal verse as the main source and extends it to the donkey

steps.title: What does our תנא do with the repeated word 'firstborn'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how our משנה's תנא uses the repeated word 'בכור', since he does not use it the way רבי יוסי הגלילי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, what does he do with this repeated 'firstborn,' 'firstborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard follow-up question. If our תנא does not learn the 'same kind' rule from the repeated word 'בכור', what does he learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. רבי יוסי הגלילי used the repetition of 'בכור' (ox, lamb, goat) for the 'same kind' rule. Our תנא learns that rule from the donkey verse, so the repeated 'בכור' still needs a job in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, the author of our משנה
What does he do with it? (How does he use this verse?)
Firstborn animal

phrases.english: And our Tanna (of the Mishnah),
this 'firstborn,' 'firstborn'
phrases.notes: The verse (במדבר יח:יז) says 'firstborn of an ox, firstborn of a lamb, firstborn of a goat.'

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how the two תנאים differ, the גמרא asks what the other תנא does with the verse he did not use.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does our תנא learn from the repeated word 'בכור', since he does not use it for the 'same kind' rule?

steps.title: He needs it for the teaching of רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא needs the repeated 'בכור' for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our תנא uses the repetition for a different lesson, one taught by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. The next step will spell out that lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse continues 'and you shall burn their fat' (the אימורין). Our תנא reads the separate mention of each animal as needed for that burning law. So the words are not extra in his view, and nothing is left over for the 'same kind' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the verse is needed for another teaching)
For the teaching of רבי...

phrases.english: He needs it
for that of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repetition is used for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching about burning the אימורין of each kind of בכור.

steps.title: Why is burning the sacrificial parts stated for each animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks why the Torah states the burning of אימורין separately for the firstborn ox, lamb, and goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Why were the אימורין stated for a firstborn ox, the אימורין for a firstborn lamb, and the אימורין for a firstborn goat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching. It opens with his question: why does the Torah need to mention all three animals for the burning of the sacrificial parts? This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think one animal would be enough, and we could learn the other two from it. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is setting up a 'צריכא' argument. He will show that each animal is needed, because each one has a special feature.

keyTerms.meaning: The sacrificial parts (fats, etc.) burned on the מזבח
Why were they stated?
Ox, lamb, goat

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Why were sacrificial parts stated for a firstborn ox,
sacrificial parts for a firstborn lamb,
and sacrificial parts for a firstborn goat?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching that step 27 pointed to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the Torah need to mention the burning of אימורין for each of the three kinds of בכור, rather than just one?

steps.title: Each is needed: an ox has more wine libations
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah wrote only the ox, we would say only an ox's אימורין are burned, because an ox gets more נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If the Torah had written it only for a firstborn ox, we would say that is because the ox has more נסכים (wine libations).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא begins answering with 'צריכא': each animal must be written. He starts with the ox. If only the ox were mentioned, we could not apply the law to the lamb and goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox offering comes with a larger amount of נסכים than a lamb or goat. So the ox seems more important, and we might think only it deserves to have its parts burned on the מזבח. That is why the ox alone would not teach us about the smaller animals.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (each case must be stated; one cannot be learned from the other)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Wine libations poured with an offering
It has more, it was given extra

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written only the firstborn ox —
[I would say that is] because it has more libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ox could not teach the others, because its extra נסכים make it special.

steps.title: A lamb has the extra fat-tail
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah wrote only the lamb, we would say only a lamb's parts are burned, because its אליה is also burned, giving it more אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lamb: because it has more, namely the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer continues with the lamb. The lamb alone would also not be enough to teach the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a sheep, the fat tail (אליה) is also offered on the מזבח, so a lamb has more burned parts than an ox or goat. That special feature means we could not learn the other animals from the lamb. The reason for the goat comes in the next lines of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat tail of a sheep, which is burned on the מזבח with the other parts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'more' here means the lamb gets more נסכים. An ox has more נסכים. A lamb has more burned parts, because its tail is included.

phrases.english: A lamb —
[I would say that is] because it has more, with the tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא argument from the ox to the lamb.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lamb could not teach the others, because its burned אליה makes it special.

steps.title: Why the goat alone would not teach the others
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written the rule only for a goat, we would say only a goat's אימורין are burned. This is because a goat has extra importance in the case of an individual who sins with עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah wrote only 'goat,' we would say the rule applies only to a goat, because a goat has an extra role: it is the offering brought by an individual who sins with idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of three reasons. Now it explains why the goat could not teach the ox and the lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual who sins by mistake usually may bring either a lamb or a goat as a חטאת. But for עבודה זרה, an individual must bring a goat specifically. That gives the goat a special status, so we could not learn the other animals from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Goat
Has been 'included more', meaning it has an extra role or importance
Idol worship
An individual person (as opposed to the whole community)

steps.whatToRemember: All three animals have a special feature: the ox gets more נסכים, the lamb has its אליה burned, and the goat is the offering for an individual's עבודה זרה. So no single animal can teach the other two.

phrases.english: [Had it written only] with regard to a goat —

phrases.english: with regard to idol worship by an individual.
phrases.notes: An individual who sins with idolatry by mistake must bring a she-goat as a חטאת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final part of the answer that began in step 29, now about the goat.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The goat needs its own verse because it alone is the offering for an individual's עבודה זרה, so it could not teach the ox and the lamb.

steps.title: Why not learn one animal from the other two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: it is true that one animal cannot be learned from just one other. But why not learn the third animal from the other two together?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, one cannot be learned from one. But let us learn one from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. It says the Torah only needed to write two animals, and we could learn the third from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 29-31 showed that no single animal can teach the others. But when two animals together point to the same rule, the special feature of each one should not matter. So it looks like one of the three verses is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: One from one: learning one case from a single other case
Cannot be derived
Let it be derived / let us learn it
From two cases together

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not taking back what it just said. It agrees that one animal cannot teach another. It is only asking about using two animals together to teach the third.

phrases.notes: Accepts the conclusion of steps 29-31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three-part answer by suggesting a learning from two cases together, which would make one verse extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all three verses (ox, lamb, goat) are needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A learning from two cases together cancels out the special feature of each single case, so only two verses should be needed.

steps.title: The ox cannot be learned from the lamb and goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by asking which verse we would leave out. If we left out the ox, we could not learn it from the lamb and goat, because both of them have a special role in the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one should the Torah not write? If the Torah did not write the ox, and we learned it from the others, we could object: the others are special because they are used for the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by testing each option. First it tries leaving out the ox, and shows that this does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן פסח can be a lamb or a goat, but never an ox. So the lamb and goat share a special feature that the ox does not have. That is why we could not learn the ox from them, and the ox needs its own verse.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to which one?

steps.title: The lamb cannot be learned from the ox and goat
steps.stepSummary: Next the גמרא tries leaving out the lamb. This also fails, because the ox and goat share a special role when the whole community sins with עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah did not write the lamb, and we learned it from the others, we could object: the others are special because they are brought when the community sins with idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues testing the options. Now it tries leaving out the lamb, and shows that this does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the whole community sins with עבודה זרה by mistake, it brings an ox as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת, but no lamb. So the ox and goat share a special feature that the lamb does not have. That means the lamb needs its own verse too.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamb / sheep
The community as a whole

steps.whyThisMatters: Each pair has a special feature that the third animal lacks. That is why even a learning from two cases fails, and all three verses are needed. This leaves room for the verses to teach the lesson of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamb could be learned from the ox and goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamb cannot be learned from the ox and goat, because both are brought for a communal sin of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Leaving out the goat also fails
steps.stepSummary: The third try: if the Torah left out the goat, we could not learn the goat from the ox and lamb, because both of them have something 'extra' on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah did not write the goat, and we learned it from the ox and lamb, that would not work. The ox and lamb are special, because each one gives the altar something extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option: leaving out the goat and learning it from the ox and lamb. It shows that this does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox and the lamb share an 'extra' feature at the מזבח. The ox gets bigger נסכים (wine and flour offerings) than a goat, and the lamb's אליה (fat tail) is burned, but a goat's is not. Since the goat lacks this extra feature, you cannot learn the goat from them.

The altar
And let it be learned from these

steps.title: All three animals are needed
steps.stepSummary: Since no animal can be learned from the other two, the Torah had to write all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, all three are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: every one of the three animals had to be written in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of animals shares some special feature that the third lacks. So none can be learned from the others, and the verse needs all three to teach the burning of the אימורין.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
They are (all) needed

steps.whatToRemember: Ox, lamb, and goat each needed their own mention. One can't be learned from one, and one can't be learned from two, since every pair shares something special.

phrases.english: Therefore, they are all necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the three-way test from Steps 33-35.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three animals must be written in the verse about burning the אימורין of a בכור.

steps.title: The repeated word 'firstborn' teaches that the baby must match its mother
steps.stepSummary: If the verse is needed for burning the parts, how does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn from it that the firstborn must match its mother? Answer: the word בכור is repeated with no need. That extra wording teaches the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn his rule? If the verse only meant to teach about burning, it should say 'But a firstborn ox, lamb, and goat.' Why does it repeat 'firstborn,' 'firstborn'? It must be to teach that it counts only when the mother is an ox and her firstborn is an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quietly asks how רבי יוסי הגלילי can use this verse, since we just showed it is needed for something else. Then it answers that the extra repeated words give him his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three animal names are needed for the burning law, but the word בכור written three times is not. One בכור could cover all three animals. The extra בכור words teach that the baby must be the same kind as its mother (an ox born from an ox).

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why do I need it? (points to extra wording)
Rather, isn't it right to learn from this
Firstborn

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method. Even when a verse is needed for one law, extra or repeated words in it can teach a second law.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili — how does he learn his rule from this verse?
phrases.notes: An implied question: the verse seems used up for the burning law.

phrases.english: If so (that it teaches only burning), let the verse write
"But a firstborn ox, lamb, and goat";
why do I need "firstborn," "firstborn" repeated?

phrases.english: only when it (the mother) is an ox and its firstborn is an ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, אִם כֵּן לִיכְתּוֹב קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the verse is shown to be needed for the burning law, the גמרא defends רבי יוסי הגלילי's use of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can רבי יוסי הגלילי learn the 'must match its mother' rule from a verse needed for burning the אימורין?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra repeated word בכור teaches that the firstborn must be the same kind as its mother.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי הגלילי do with 'פטר חמור' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The other view learns the 'match its mother' rule from the double phrase פטר חמור. So what does רבי יוסי הגלילי use that phrase for?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי, what does he do with the phrase 'firstborn of a donkey,' 'firstborn of a donkey'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the phrase פטר חמור, written twice in the Torah. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא of the משנה learns the 'match its mother' rule from the double פטר חמור. רבי יוסי הגלילי gets that rule from the extra בכור words instead. So we expect him to use the phrase פטר חמור for some other teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The firstborn of a donkey (it must be redeemed)
What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי יוסי הגלילי learns his rule from 'בכור', the גמרא asks what he learns from the verse the משנה uses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn from the double phrase פטר חמור?

steps.title: 'פטר חמור' limits redemption to donkeys
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי needs פטר חמור for a ברייתא. A verse says to redeem 'the firstborn of an impure animal,' which could include horses and camels. The phrase פטר חמור teaches that only a donkey's firstborn is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: the verse says 'redeem the firstborn of man, and redeem the firstborn of the impure animal.' I might think this includes firstborn horses and camels. So the verse says 'firstborn of a donkey': I told you a donkey's firstborn, not horses' and camels'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי uses פטר חמור to limit the מצוה of redemption to donkeys only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in במדבר says 'בכור הבהמה הטמאה' (an impure animal's firstborn). That sounds like every non-kosher animal. The phrase פטר חמור narrows it, so only a firstborn donkey needs redemption, not a horse or a camel.

keyTerms.meaning: For that which is taught in a ברייתא
You shall surely redeem
A non-kosher animal
I might understand (a possible wrong reading)
The verse teaches (to correct that reading)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the extra בכור words teach that the baby must match its mother. פטר חמור teaches that, among non-kosher animals, only donkeys are redeemed.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בהמה טמאה' here does not mean ritual impurity (טומאה). It means a non-kosher animal.

steps.title: Maybe horses and camels are still redeemed, just not with a lamb
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on its own conclusion. Maybe פטר חמור only limits the lamb redemption to donkeys, while firstborn horses and camels are still redeemed with any item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I can still say: firstborn donkeys are redeemed with a lamb, and firstborn horses and camels are redeemed with anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own conclusion from step 39. It suggests that the verse may not exclude horses and camels from redemption at all. This sets up the next move, where the ברייתא will reject this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 39, פטר חמור was read as 'only a donkey is redeemed, not other impure animals.' The new suggestion reads it more narrowly: 'only a donkey is redeemed with a שה.' On that reading, horses and camels would still need redemption, just with any item of value. So the verse alone has not yet proven that horses and camels are fully exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And still I can say.' A ברייתא formula that raises another possible reading after a first conclusion
Firstborn donkeys
A lamb or kid. The required item for redeeming a firstborn donkey
Horses and camels. Other impure animals that might have been included
With any item. Redemption with anything of value, not only a lamb

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. It is a suggestion that the ברייתא raises so that it can reject it. In the end, only a donkey's firstborn needs redemption at all.

phrases.english: And still I can say:
phrases.notes: Signals a new doubt about the conclusion just reached.

phrases.notes: The verse would only limit the lamb rule to donkeys.

phrases.english: firstborn horses and camels are redeemed with any item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading from step 39 that פטר חמור excludes horses and camels from redemption altogether.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that פטר חמור teaches that only a donkey's firstborn is redeemed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase could limit only the method of redemption (a שה) to donkeys. It would not exclude other impure animals from needing redemption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Horses and camels are redeemed with any item of value, and only donkeys need a שה.
